document_metadata.title: 11、INT. UCLA SCREENING ROOM - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Jim's student film sparks heated debate over art and shock value; faculty and peers clash in criticism and defense, leading Jim to quit after refusing to justify his work.

entities.name: Student film projects disturbing montage of sexuality and Nazi imagery
entities.description: A 16mm black and white student film displays a sequence beginning with a blond woman dancing on a TV in lingerie, then pans to footage of Nazi goose-stepping and a Nuremberg rally, accompanied by sounds of lovemaking and an Indian peyote ceremony.

entities.name: Jim's voiceover delivers philosophical narration over film
entities.description: Jim's voice is heard on the soundtrack quoting Nietzsche and inviting listeners to attend to the 'sound of the Nuremberg night,' blending mystical and poetic imagery.

entities.name: Students react negatively to the film's pretentious tone
entities.description: Audience members, identified as students, groan and express disdain for the perceived pretension of the film and its narration.

entities.name: Closeup of Jim appears on screen taking a hit from a hash pipe
entities.description: A closeup shot shows Jim on screen staring directly into the camera as he inhales from a hash pipe and winks, symbolizing rebellion and altered consciousness.

entities.name: Jim's on-screen persona describes mystical experiences through the senses
entities.description: Jim's voice on the film answers the question 'Have you ever seen God?' by describing visions, sensations, sounds, touch, and taste associated with divine experience.

entities.name: Students heckle and dismiss the film as an ego trip
entities.description: Following the screening, students ad-lib derogatory comments such as 'ego trip man' and 'SSSSssss,' expressing mockery and rejection of the work.

entities.name: Ray Manzarek defends the film to Jim
entities.description: Ray Manzarek, a fellow student, leans over to Jim and praises the film as 'great,' describing it as non-linear poetry in the style of Godard, offering encouragement amid criticism.

entities.name: Lights come on after the film ends with absurdist imagery
entities.description: The theater lights illuminate as the final surreal images of the film flicker out, marking the end of the screening.

entities.name: Audience responds with hissing and a Bronx cheer
entities.description: Approximately 100 students in the bunker-like theater react to the film's conclusion with audible disapproval, including hissing and a loud Bronx cheer.

entities.name: Underground Student Film Screening
entities.description: An informal gathering of students in a bunker-like theater to view and react to an avant-garde 16mm student film blending erotic, political, and psychedelic themes.
entities.summary: An informal gathering of students in a bunker-like theater to view and react to an avant-garde 16mm student film blending erotic, political, and psychedelic themes.

entities.name: bunker-like theater
entities.description: A physical, enclosed setting where the student film screening takes place, described with a specific atmospheric quality.

entities.name: Jim
entities.description: A student filmmaker whose voiceover and on-screen persona present philosophical and mystical reflections during the screening of his film.
entities.summary: A young boy witnesses a traumatic highway accident involving a truck carrying Native Americans, marking his first encounter with death, while a man in torn black chinos observes the scene, reflecting on fear and human connection.

entities.name: Ray Manzarek
entities.description: A tall student with a powerful voice and manner, wearing thick glasses and long hair, who defends Jim's film as poetic and non-linear.
entities.summary: A tall, bespectacled keyboardist in The Doors, known for his poetic insight, flamboyant piano playing, and calm demeanor, participates in a countercultural wedding and reflects on rock as a ritualistic art form.

entities.name: Blond dancer
entities.description: A striking woman in a black bra, panties, garters, and heels who dances on top of a TV set in the student film.

entities.name: hash pipe
entities.description: A smoking device used by Jim in a closeup scene where he takes a hit and winks at the camera.

entities.name: Nazi imagery
entities.description: Visual motifs including goose-stepping Nazis and a Nuremberg rally incorporated into the student film to evoke shock and symbolic meaning.

entities.name: Indian peyote ceremony
entities.description: A spiritual ritual referenced in the film's audio track, featuring an incanting holy man and associated with hallucinogenic experience.

entities.name: non-linear film
entities.description: An experimental cinematic form celebrated as poetic and abstract, exemplified by Godard and referenced in defense of the student film.

entities.name: Instructor confronts Jim Morrison about the film's shock value and artistic merit
entities.description: The instructor addresses Jim Morrison directly, criticizing the use of Naziism and masturbation for shock value and questioning the artistic intention behind the film.

entities.name: Student interrupts to call the film boring and pretentious
entities.description: A student loudly declares the film to be a bore, prompting laughter from the audience and escalating the debate over its artistic value.

entities.name: Trick defends the film by comparing it favorably to a Warhol picture
entities.description: Trick, one of Jim's friends, raises his hand and argues that the film is better than an Andy Warhol piece, attempting to justify its avant-garde nature.

entities.name: Girl反驳s Trick's defense by claiming the film is worse than Warhol
entities.description: A girl in the audience challenges Trick's comparison, asserting that the film is not only worse than a Warhol picture but fundamentally lacking in artistic or political substance.

entities.name: Students argue about political consciousness and pretentiousness in the film
entities.description: Multiple students voice their opinions, criticizing the film for lacking political awareness and equating its style with excessive pretension.

entities.name: Jack accuses critics of being fascists for dismissing the film
entities.description: Jack, another of Jim's friends, reacts defensively to the criticism, turning the accusation around by labeling the detractors as fascists.

entities.name: Bones defends the film as taking genitalism to absurdity
entities.description: Bones argues that the film pushes themes of sexuality to an absurd extreme, suggesting that the audience's discomfort stems from the film school's conservative mindset.

entities.name: Audience members shout down the defenders with mockery and dismissive chants
entities.description: A wave of hostile voices interrupts the debate, with audience members yelling 'Boo!', 'Beatniks go home!', and 'Take another mushroom' to ridicule the film and its supporters.

entities.name: Instructor restores order and asks Jim Morrison for his feelings
entities.description: The instructor calls for silence and directly asks Jim Morrison to respond to the criticism, seeking his personal reaction to the audience's response.

entities.name: Jim Morrison declares 'I quit' and walks out of the screening
entities.description: Overwhelmed or defiant, Jim Morrison responds to the hostile reception by announcing he quits and exits the theater abruptly.

entities.name: Instructor
entities.description: A faculty member who leads the discussion after the film screening and challenges Jim Morrison about the artistic merit and shock value of his work.

document_metadata.title: 21、EXT. VENICE ROOFTOP - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Jim and Ray, having named their band 'The Doors,' plan rehearsals and move in together, envisioning transformative music as they walk along the Pacific, inspired by myth and counterculture.

entities.name: Ray attempts meditation without success
entities.description: Ray tries to meditate but is visibly frustrated, shaking his head and frowning, unable to achieve a state of bliss.

entities.name: Jim approaches and teases Ray about using acid
entities.description: Jim comes closer to Ray, amused, and suggests taking LSD as a more reliable path to transcendence than meditation.

entities.name: Ray expresses discomfort from past psychedelic experience
entities.description: Ray opens his eyes, recognizes Jim, and describes a previous bad trip in which he felt like he was in hell, visualizing imagery reminiscent of Hieronymus Bosch.

entities.name: Jim claims he never had a bad experience on acid
entities.description: Jim responds to Ray's story by asserting that he has never had a negative trip on LSD, reinforcing his positive view of psychedelics.

entities.name: Ray recounts failed meeting with MGM production head
entities.description: Ray describes how he tried to advocate for Godard's improvisational filmmaking style to the head of production at MGM, who responded with ignorance about who Godard was.

entities.name: Jim declares intent to reinvent cultural myths
entities.description: Jim expresses a visionary idea about reclaiming the planet and creating new gods and myths through cultural transformation.

entities.name: Jim reveals he got lost in the desert and lived on Trick's rooftop
entities.description: Jim explains that instead of going to New York, he ended up stranded in the desert for days and has since been living on a rooftop, emotionally stuck on a woman.

entities.name: Jim shares that he has been writing poems and songs
entities.description: Jim tells Ray that during his time on the rooftop, he has been creatively active, writing poetry and song lyrics.

entities.name: Ray requests to hear one of Jim's songs
entities.description: Ray shows interest in Jim's creative work and asks him to perform one of his songs, despite Jim's hesitation.

entities.name: Ray quotes Bob Dylan to encourage Jim
entities.description: Ray recites lyrics from a Bob Dylan song to argue that lyrical content matters more than vocal ability, using Dylan as an example.

entities.description: A cinematic approach associated with directors like Godard, where scripts are eschewed in favor of spontaneous creation, referenced in Ray's anecdote about MGM.

entities.name: Jim performs an impromptu song about swimming to the moon
entities.description: Jim suddenly begins singing lyrics about swimming to the moon and climbing through the tide, while crouched and letting sand run through his fingers, creating a poetic and mystical atmosphere.

entities.name: Ray reacts with awe to Jim's lyrics and praises their quality
entities.description: After Jim finishes singing, Ray expresses strong admiration, calling the lyrics 'hot' and showing genuine excitement about their potential.

entities.name: Jim asks Ray to compose music for his song on the organ
entities.description: Jim proposes that Ray write musical accompaniment for the song he just performed, suggesting they go to Ray's place to work on it using Ray's organ.

entities.name: Ray enthusiastically agrees to collaborate and suggests forming a band
entities.description: Ray responds with great excitement, offering to compose the music and proposing that they form a rock and roll band together to make a million dollars.

entities.name: Jim reveals he hears music internally as if at a rock concert
entities.description: Jim explains that his songwriting process feels like taking notes at a continuous internal rock concert, where he clearly hears the music and is inspired by a sense of spiritual intoxication.

entities.name: Ray compares Jim's voice to Chet Baker and inquires about his desert experience
entities.description: Ray compliments Jim's vocal quality by likening it to jazz singer Chet Baker and presses Jim for details about what transformed him during his time in the desert.

entities.name: Ray proposes collaborating with members of his existing band
entities.description: Ray mentions that two members of his band, Robbie and John, who also meditate with him, would be interested in joining the project, suggesting a quick timeline to complete the work.

entities.name: Jim agrees to co-write songs with Ray and his bandmates
entities.description: In response to Ray's proposal, Jim expresses openness to collaborating creatively with Ray and the other musicians to develop songs together.

document_metadata.title: 31、EXT. DESERT - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Jim leaves the group alone, overwhelmed by fear and pain, as visions and voices haunt him; Pamela calls desperately, but he moves forward into a surreal, desolate landscape, seeking freedom amidst inner turmoil.

entities.name: Red Chevrolet fishtails on dry mudflat creating dust devils
entities.description: A dented red Chevrolet loses traction and slides sideways across a dry mudflat, kicking up swirling dust devils in the arid landscape.

entities.name: The Doors laugh in a circle under peyote influence
entities.description: Ray, John, Robbie, and Jim—The Doors—form a circle on the edge of a cliff, laughing intensely as the initial effects of peyote take hold, marking the beginning of a psychedelic experience.

entities.name: Pam vomits while Dorothy comforts her on cliff edge
entities.description: Pam becomes violently ill and vomits repeatedly at the edge of a cliff, while Dorothy stays by her side attempting to comfort her during the distressing episode.

entities.name: Jim climbs dune and checks on group's well-being
entities.description: Jim ascends a sand dune with panther-like movement, then asks the group if everyone is having a good time, receiving affirmations before embracing Pam.

entities.name: Jim and Pam touch intimately amid shifting shadows
entities.description: Jim and Pam engage in intimate physical contact on the dune, their faces close, shadows shifting around them as sand slowly trickles from Pam's hand.

entities.name: Jim reacts to bird and exclaims 'Hawk! Hawk!'
entities.description: Jim turns his attention to a bird in flight and shouts 'Hawk! Hawk!' with sudden intensity, indicating a heightened sensory or hallucinatory perception.

entities.name: Pam dances alone on the dune
entities.description: Pam moves rhythmically by herself on the sand dune, dancing in isolation as the psychedelic experience continues to unfold around her.

entities.name: Jim torn between group and Pam during psychedelic experience
entities.description: Jim shifts abruptly back to the circle with The Doors, visibly conflicted or divided in attention between his bandmates and his connection with Pam.

entities.name: Faces of The Doors show transition from laughter to tension
entities.description: Extreme close-ups reveal the faces of The Doors—John, Robbie, Ray, and Jim—their expressions shifting from laughter to intense psychological strain as the trip turns darker.

entities.name: Jim describes vision of giant serpent consuming consciousness
entities.description: Jim narrates a hallucinated vision of a colossal serpent with a ten-foot-long head, one red and one green eye, moving forward and devouring all consciousness and history inscribed on its scales.

entities.name: John, Robbie, and Ray shudder in reaction to Jim's vision
entities.description: John, Robbie, and Ray physically react with shudders to Jim's intense description of the serpent, reflecting their shared psychological unease and immersion in the hallucinatory atmosphere.

entities.description: A group of individuals, including members of The Doors, gather in a remote desert landscape for a psychedelic experience induced by peyote, involving visions, emotional extremes, and altered states of consciousness.

entities.name: John expresses disorientation and fear at Jim's altered state

entities.description: Jim responds to John's fear by affirming that God is partly insane, invoking Dionysus as a deity of both ecstasy and madness, normalizing the chaos as part of creation.

entities.description: Robbie tearfully confesses his terror at the limitless possibilities of existence, feeling that no one cares whether he lives or dies, expressing profound existential dread.

entities.name: Jim commands Robbie to embrace death as a possibility
entities.description: In response to Robbie's crisis, Jim simply says 'Die Robbie,' urging him to accept death as a valid existential option within the psychedelic experience.

document_metadata.title: 31、EXT. DESERT - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Jim leaves the group alone, overwhelmed by fear and pain, as visions and voices haunt him; Pamela calls desperately, but he moves forward into a surreal, desolate landscape, seeking freedom amidst inner turmoil.

entities.name: Ray expresses feelings of isolation and pain during a psychedelic experience
entities.description: Ray, overwhelmed by emotional distress, reveals his inner turmoil while under the influence of peyote, describing a profound sense of separation despite perceiving cosmic order.

entities.name: Jim affirms the value of pain as a source of aliveness
entities.description: Jim responds to Ray's suffering by asserting that pain is essential for awakening consciousness and criticizes societal tendencies to suppress it.

entities.name: John confesses overwhelming lust and internal conflict
entities.description: John admits to being consumed by sexual desire, acknowledging its insatiability and linking it to his Catholic guilt, revealing deep psychological tension.

entities.name: Jim provokes John by revealing Pam's desire and urging defiance of guilt
entities.description: Jim tells John that Pam wants him and encourages him to embrace his desires as an act of rebellion against religious shame, framing it as a way to 'fuck death away'.

entities.name: Robbie admits paralyzing fear and emotional numbness
entities.description: Robbie shares his deep-seated fears of his father and of Yahweh, confessing that he shuts down emotionally and longs to play his guitar as a form of release.

entities.name: Jim urges Robbie to confront and symbolically kill his father
entities.description: Jim challenges Robbie to overcome his fear by advocating for the symbolic or literal killing of his abusive father, framing it as a path to liberation.

entities.name: Jim calls for full emotional acceptance as a path to freedom
entities.description: Jim delivers a passionate speech urging the group to embrace all emotions—fear, pain, lust—without shame, declaring emotional authenticity as the foundation of true freedom.

entities.name: Jim re-forms the group circle by taking Ray and Robbie's hands
entities.description: In a gesture of unity and support, Jim physically reconnects with Ray and Robbie, calming them and restoring the group's cohesion through touch and presence.

entities.name: John resists joining the circle, expressing fear and impending blindness
entities.description: John remains hesitant to join the group, suffering from cold sweats and fear, and voices his belief that he will not survive the experience as his vision deteriorates.

entities.name: Jim reassures John and invites him into a tribal bond of shared strength
entities.description: Jim comforts John by affirming their collective power, declaring them a tribe of warriors united by a common spiritual source, and urging him to trust and join.

entities.name: Jim pulls John into the circle, forming a unified group on the desert floor
entities.description: Jim physically draws John into the circle, completing the group's bond as all four lower their heads to the ground in a moment of spiritual surrender and connection.

entities.name: Jim initiates a primal chant with Indian-inspired sounds and humming
entities.description: Jim begins making deep-throated 'shoooh' sounds and hums a desert song, starting a ritualistic vocalization that evokes indigenous spiritual imagery.

entities.name: The group joins in a collective chant, moving in rhythmic unison
entities.description: All four participants begin chanting together, their bodies rising and falling in sync like a single breathing entity, creating a powerful sense of unity and ritual.

entities.name: Psychedelic Vision Quest In The Desert
entities.description: A ritualistic gathering in the desert where four men, under the influence of peyote, engage in intense emotional confession, spiritual exploration, and collective chanting as part of a transformative experience.
entities.summary: A ritualistic gathering in the desert where four men, under the influence of peyote, engage in intense emotional confession, spiritual exploration, and collective chanting as part of a transformative experience.

entities.name: Ray
entities.description: A participant in a psychedelic vision quest who expresses deep feelings of isolation and pain despite perceiving the universe as functioning perfectly.
entities.summary: A group engages in a dynamic musical and philosophical exchange, with members guiding rhythm, questioning ideas, and managing interpersonal tensions, while one remains silent but perceived as domineering.

entities.name: Jim
entities.description: A central figure in the group who guides others through emotional confrontation, advocating for full acceptance of pain, fear, and lust as paths to freedom and aliveness.
entities.summary: A young boy witnesses a traumatic highway accident involving a truck carrying Native Americans, marking his first encounter with death, while a man in torn black chinos observes the scene, reflecting on fear and human connection.

entities.name: John
entities.description: A man struggling with intense lust and Catholic guilt, who fears impending blindness and hesitates to join the group's spiritual bonding.
entities.summary: Individual involved in studio management, band collaboration, and musical exercises; addresses lighting, prevents Jim from falling, critiques sound, and engages in group dynamics with Ray and other members.

entities.name: Robbie
entities.description: A man overwhelmed by fear, particularly of his father and Yahweh, leading to emotional numbness and a desire to play guitar as a form of expression.
entities.summary: A band member involved in a chaotic incident with Jim contributes musically by introducing 'Light My Fire,' reflects on personal thoughts during performance, and helps pack equipment afterward, while noting Jim's romantic appeal.

entities.summary: A woman interacts with Jim on a balcony, shares personal reflections on a rooftop, and joins him on a playful night walk, revealing emotional vulnerability and spiritual insights while forming a tentative connection.

entities.name: Catholic guilt
entities.description: A moral and emotional framework tied to John's internal conflict, representing the psychological burden of religious shame around desire.

entities.description: A symbolic social identity proposed by Jim, representing a bonded group drawing strength from shared experience and a common spiritual source.

document_metadata.title: 57、INT. ROOM - LIMBO
document_metadata.summary: Jim searches for Nico amid a surreal, chaotic party, distracted by fans and warped reflections of himself, while being guided toward Andy Warhol, his bandmates having left and band unity fraying.

entities.name: PR man insists Jim meet Andy Warhol
entities.description: A public relations man grabs Jim's arm and enthusiastically urges him to meet Andy Warhol, describing Warhol as more than an artist—'Andy is art'—and framing the encounter as a meeting of two cultural icons.

entities.name: Pamela introduces Tom Baker and Count Ruspoli to Jim
entities.description: Pamela excitedly introduces Jim to Tom Baker, a charismatic actor who appeared in one of Andy Warhol's films, and Count Ruspoli, an Italian aristocrat from a historic family, emphasizing their status and connections.

entities.name: Tom Baker offers Jim drugs after complimenting his performance
entities.description: After complimenting Jim on his recent gig at 'The Scene', Tom Baker offers him multiple substances—including a pill, popper, joint, and drink—suggesting he is heavily under the influence and immersed in the drug-fueled scene.

entities.name: Ray urges Jim to leave the gathering
entities.description: Ray interrupts the interactions, insisting that Jim come with him because they are leaving, mentioning that Dorothy is waiting and they plan to eat at Max's.

entities.name: John Densmore arrives with Robbie and a new girlfriend
entities.description: John Densmore appears at the scene accompanied by a visibly high and giggling Robbie and a new female companion, expressing discomfort with the atmosphere by calling it 'fucking weird'.

document_metadata.title: 57、INT. ROOM - LIMBO
document_metadata.summary: Jim searches for Nico amid a surreal, chaotic party, distracted by fans and warped reflections of himself, while being guided toward Andy Warhol, his bandmates having left and band unity fraying.

entities.name: Ray rejects Jim's plea and asserts the group's need to stay together

entities.description: In a moment of slow motion, Ray taps Jim's shoulder in goodbye, representing a deeper, almost ritualistic parting.

document_metadata.summary: Andy Warhol gives Jim a gold telephone, saying it allows communication with God, then disappears; Jim is summoned by Nico as Doors' song plays, emphasizing fleeting fame and isolation.

document_metadata.title: 102、INT. AIRPLANE - THAT NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Jim and Tom escalate into a food fight, provoking crew intervention; the captain threatens arrest, met with sarcastic compliance as chaos disrupts the flight.

entities.name: Tom confronts Jim with cruel sarcasm about his isolation
entities.description: Tom mocks Jim, telling him he is alone and feared by others due to his erratic behavior, emphasizing that only Tom remains by his side.

entities.name: Jim claims his actions were driven by a pursuit of freedom
entities.description: In response to Tom's taunts, Jim denies being mad and asserts that his motivations have been about seeking freedom, not chaos.

entities.name: Tom accuses Jim of boredom and failed rebellion
entities.description: Tom dismisses Jim's claim of seeking freedom, arguing that he has merely exhausted all indulgences—fame, sex, money—and now faces irrelevance.

entities.name: Jim challenges Tom's understanding of the audience's desires
entities.description: Jim lashes back at Tom, accusing him of underestimating people and misunderstanding what they truly seek in life.

entities.description: In a quiet, intense moment, Jim whispers that what people truly desire is not material success but something sacred, framing it as the core human yearning.

document_metadata.title: 107、INT. STAGE - SAME NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Amid chaos and a collapsing show, authorities search for Jim Morrison as the band's live era ends in debris and disillusionment.

entities.name: The Doors begin performing 'Five to One'
entities.description: The band starts playing the ominous introductory strains of 'Five to One' in an attempt to shift focus from Jim and launch the concert performance.

entities.name: Crowd demands the doors be opened
entities.description: The audience chants repeatedly for the doors to open, creating an intense and overwhelming atmosphere of anticipation and frenzy.

entities.name: Jim picks up a joint thrown on stage
entities.description: Jim, in a regal gesture, bends down to pick up a marijuana joint that has been thrown at his feet by the audience.

entities.name: Jim lights a joint on stage
entities.description: Jim ignites a marijuana joint in front of the audience, contributing to the escalating tension and illicit energy of the performance.

entities.description: As the music progresses, the crowd synchronizes their foot stomping in a primal, rhythmic response to the beat of the song.

entities.description: Audience members throw personal items such as bras onto the stage, while others run through the venue with sparklers, heightening the chaotic spectacle.

entities.name: Jim struggles to start singing lyrics
entities.description: Due to being drunk and high, Jim fails to begin the lyrics immediately, forcing the band to loop the musical beat repeatedly.

entities.name: Jim reacts to microphone as if shocked
entities.description: Jim jerks his hand away from the microphone suddenly, mimicking the sensation of touching a live electrical wire.

entities.name: Crowd shouts encouragement to Jim
entities.description: The audience erupts in a collective scream, demanding 'ARE YOU READY' and building dramatic tension before the performance resumes.

entities.name: Jim flicks joint into crowd to evade police
entities.description: As an officer approaches to confront him about the drug, Jim calmly tosses the joint back into the audience, avoiding immediate arrest.

entities.name: Teenager jumps from balcony into crowd
entities.description: A teenage fan stands on a balcony railing and dramatically dives 18 feet into the audience below, landing safely amid the throng.

entities.name: Cops rush to respond to balcony jumper
entities.description: Law enforcement personnel quickly move toward the location where the teenager landed after jumping from the balcony.

entities.name: Teenager stands up unharmed and flees
entities.description: After landing in the crowd, the teenager rises with a dazed expression, exclaims 'Wow!', and runs off, pursued by confused officers.

entities.name: Jim unleashes a primal scream
entities.description: Jim releases one of his signature intense, raw vocal screams, reigniting the crowd's energy and drawing attention back to the stage.
